content:
This is about a general question about how to best formalise problems of the type:
"Is there an algorithm/Turing machine/decision procedure to decide X"

Two examples are

  • FC#2175 "Coxeter Group Isomorphism Problem"
  • FC#3495 "Short polynomial containment decidability"

The second one uses ComputablePred and make sense to me, not sure how to do the first one best.

I'd love if somebody else could take a look here!
Who would be good to review this?

I have little experience with lean so far, but what I read here https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/Computability/Halting.html is exactly what I have in mind: Find some reduction so that one could solve the Halting problem if one could decide 3-term-polynomial containment.

I feel like this is a general problem with classical math and constructive math. If a problem specifically asks for a construction / witness, then we cant just allow Classical as there is always the option of a Nonconstructive Proof.

In FC#2175 "Coxeter Group Isomorphism Problem", the problem asks specifically about giving / witnessing a decision procedure.

I have also opened FC#3524, where the problem asks for a construction of a Steiner System (under certain constraints). There are also nonconstructive theorems, about the existence of Steiner Systems, but those would be "research solved".

How should we handle Constructive / Witness Problems? Or how do we currently handle them?
Would it make sense to have it as convention to allow "def ..." only for constructive problems. Or is there a technical obstacle to that convention?
